raw_response:
I'm a 58-year-old woman who's been farming these 10 mu for 40 years. I finished senior high school — unusual for my generation in the village — and I pay attention to the extension bulletins. But I'm not running a business farm; it's just me and my husband, and our son works in Shijiazhuang, so we're down to two people for all the field work. Every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back, or we feel it.

It's early October now. The maize came off last week — about 480 kg per mu, decent but not great because August was dry and I only irrigated twice. The stalks are shredded and the field needs turning. I hired Old Wang's tractor for rotary tillage (80 yuan per mu) because we can't manage that by hand anymore, and I'll plant wheat in the next few days.

For the wheat, I'm using my own saved seed from the batch I bought two years ago — a semi-dwarf variety that doesn't lodge. I seed at about 15 kg per mu. The soil is still carrying some fertility from the maize residue, but I know from last year that I can't cut back too much. I'm putting down a compound fertilizer base: roughly 50 kg of 15-15-15 per mu, which gives me about 7.5 kg N, 7.5 kg P₂O₅, and 7.5 kg K₂O. Then at jointing in March, if the wheat looks green and the weather forecast is decent, I'll topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu — that's another 9 kg N. So total N around 16–17 kg per mu. I used to do more, but at 2.4 yuan per kg for urea and compound at 3.2 yuan, the numbers add up fast.

Water is metered and expensive from the tube well — about 35 yuan per irrigation per mu. I'll irrigate three times: once in November before winter if it's dry, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Four would be better, but my husband's factory job doesn't give him flexible leave, so I have to time irrigations when he's home to help manage the pump and pipes. Three is what we can manage.

For maize next June, the window will be brutal — usually less than a week between wheat harvest and planting. I'll buy fresh hybrid seed; never save maize seed, everyone knows the yield crashes. I plant at about 2.5 kg per mu, density around 4,500 plants. Base fertilizer will go down at planting: roughly 40 kg of compound per mu, then topdress with 25 kg urea at big trumpet stage if the rains don't come. Two irrigations for maize — one at jointing and one at filling, but only if there's no rain. Sometimes we get lucky with summer showers.

Pesticides: I spray herbicide on wheat in early spring (broadleaf weeds are bad in this field), and for maize I use a pre-emergence herbicide and maybe one insecticide spray if I see corn borer in July. That's usually enough.

Labor is our real constraint. Between us two, we can handle the spraying, fertilizing, and day-to-day irrigation, but for wheat harvest and maize harvest I hire 3–4 days of custom combine and a couple days of hired labor for hauling and bagging. Hired labor is 120 yuan per day now.

I'm targeting 450 kg per mu for wheat and 500 kg per mu for maize. If wheat prices stay around 2.4 yuan per kg and maize around 2.2, that gives us roughly 21,000 yuan gross. After inputs, maybe 15,000 yuan left — not counting our labor, of course. It's enough, but there's no room to waste money.
